lines: Meet The RM Assistant: one AI assistant for every relationship manager, starting each day on Today.
You're Jordan Ellis, a relationship manager with twelve business clients, all sample data.
Each Monday starts here: the clients worth a call this week.
First, the Signal Finder runs plain rules the business owns, like idle cash, and reads real Federal Reserve rate data.
Then Claude explains each one in plain English, and every number is checked. Anything it can't trace is flagged.
Jordan decides: use it, change it, or reject it. Using it creates an AI-sourced opportunity, so results can be counted.
Before Tuesday's meeting, it checks four sources and writes a one-page brief, with a source on every fact.
After the meeting, it drafts the recap, email and CRM note from Jordan's notes. No recording without the client's consent.
Nothing is saved or sent until Jordan approves. Anything unclear comes back marked check, instead of guessed.
Coming in wave two: early warning flags clients who may be drifting away. It's a reason to call, never a credit signal.
It also spots needs the treasury team serves, and drafts the hand-off. Jordan sends it, and it's tracked to accepted.
Try to break it. Ask for a credit decision, a price, or another banker's client, and the guardrails stop it before any AI sees it.
Five measures from day one: usage, quality, business impact, adoption, and risk. A pilot compares bankers with and without the assistant.
A pilot needs client data, a risk partner from day one, and a few relationship managers. Our assumption, to confirm: data access sets the pace.
Now it's your turn: start from Today, and run the agents live on Claude.
